findings.title: Length-normalized loss does not inherit SIC reference endpoint
findings.assumptions: Finite two-response action set, lengths 1 and 2, full-support reference (1/2,1/2), zero margin rewards and unrestricted Bernoulli policy. No infinite-support or partition issues.
findings.decisive_evidence: The reference-dominant term is -.5 log(t)-.25 log(1-t), uniquely minimized at t=2/3, whereas the stated original KL objective is minimized at t=1/2 for every lambda. General limit proportional to q_y/length_y.
findings.alternative_readings: First-KL approximation is acknowledged but no SIC-preserving bound supplied. Equal lengths avoid the reference-endpoint counterexample; reward temperature still changes under a common length. Actual Ehrlich benchmark outputs not asserted to match toy action space.
findings.core_dependency: Pure KL SIC proof is invoked for modified MargE objective and SIC interpretation of ablation.
findings.impact: Core theoretical property is not inherited by practical loss; experimental curves not refuted.
findings.correction: Exact finite full-support KL objective has valid endpoint limits; removing length factors restores that objective. No practical estimator or length-control repair certified.

findings.title: Reproduction configuration makes direct reward gradient vanish
findings.assumptions: Supplied decoder-only reproduction path, local microbatch 1, finite positive ratios, self_normalize_weights True, code alpha 1 and beta 10.
findings.decisive_evidence: w/sum(w)=1 with zero derivative, so loss=-9 log(p)/length-r and reward does not influence the update. Accumulation and DDP average already-computed gradients. Independent finite differences give same gradient -.2109375 for rewards 0,.5,1.
findings.alternative_readings: Reward still affects data-pair selection and possibly checkpoint choice. Historical larger microbatches or overrides could avoid this; connection to original curves unverified.
findings.core_dependency: README-designated MargE reproduction path loses central direct reward-magnitude training mechanism.
findings.impact: Major in supplied core implementation/configuration; not proof that historical benchmark figures used it.
findings.correction: Requires properly defined normalization across multiple examples and valid estimator/proposal law; changing accumulation alone insufficient. No distributed training repair executed.

findings.title: Released REINFORCE ablation omits stated importance weights
findings.assumptions: Fixed off-policy training data, two responses, proposal (.9,.1), rewards (.5,1); zero reference coefficient used to isolate data term.
findings.decisive_evidence: Returned unweighted reward log-likelihood has optimum (9/11,2/11), versus expected-reward optimum (0,1). Branch ignores its ratio argument.
findings.alternative_readings: On-policy sampling would justify a different estimator, but inspected branch is fixed-data. Historical run identity unknown.
findings.core_dependency: Local control used to assess SIC; actual Figure 5c material impact unresolved.
findings.impact: Supported released-ablation mismatch, with historical scientific effect Needs Evidence.
findings.correction: Specify proposal and score-function differentiation before restoring off-policy control; full ablation not repaired or rerun.
